procedural_history.originating_court: Calcutta High Court exercising its Ordinary Original Civil Jurisdiction
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated the 9th day of June 1952 of the Calcutta High Court in Appeal No. 26 of 1952
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The case originated in the Calcutta High Court under its Ordinary Original Civil Jurisdiction in Matter No. 110 of 1950. An order was issued on December 6, 1951. This order was then appealed (Appeal No. 26 of 1952) within the Calcutta High Court, resulting in a Judgment and Order dated June 9, 1952.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Judgment and Order dated June 9, 1952 of the Calcutta High Court was appealed to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court heard Civil Appeals Nos. 9 and 10 of 1954.

issue.issue_text: Whether sales tax is payable on the sale in question.

facts: The Government of India's Ministry of Industry and Supplies purchased a large quantity of hessian cloth from a company referred to as "the Mills".

The contract specified that the prices were exclusive of Bengal Sales Tax and that the Government of India would pay the tax directly to the West Bengal government "if it is ultimately found that sales tax is payable".
The Commercial Tax Officer assessed the Mills for sales tax on this transaction.
The Mills contested the assessment, arguing that the sale was exempt from tax.
law: The central legal question was the applicability of the exemption clause found in section 5(2)(a)(iii) of the Bengal Finance (Sales Tax) Act, 1941.
application: The Mills claimed the benefit of the exemption under section 5(2)(a)(iii) of the Act to argue that no tax was due.
The case went through the Calcutta High Court, where a Single Judge initially ruled in favor of the Mills, but a Division Bench on appeal reversed that decision, finding the tax was payable.
The Supreme Court then heard the appeal, focusing solely on whether the exemption in the Act applied to this specific sale.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the sales of hessian made to the Ministry of Industries and Supplies of the Government of India were not exempt from payment of sales tax under the Act. The Court affirmed the lower court's decision, holding that the State of West Bengal was entitled to levy the tax and that the sales tax was payable on the transaction. Consequently, the appeals were dismissed.
